body:
D-HOE-20261030-04: test-infra, signal only recorded PIDs (M1, m7 from `engineering/reviews/ui-qa-run-rc-lane-harness-8bd8fb46-architect.md`). Base `rc/v5` @ 2fa7318 (rc/v5 **not** merged in, per HoE).

**Round 2:** this fixes UI QA's FAIL at 58ad41b (`qa/m3-recheck/pr89-58ad41b-static.md`): F1, F2, F3, F4, F6 and F7, plus N1 and N2. It also meets HoO's three conditions on F5. F8 is out of scope; it is an N-M2 item that stays with the harness. HoE lifted the freeze for this fix only. Head: `a32faeb`.

## Design
- **M1 (unchanged choice): an identity guard inside the repo, not lane-run/lane-kill.**
  - `scripts/recorded-pid.mjs` records a process at spawn: its pid, start time (field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`) and the boot id. The parent is always `process.pid`, and there is no parent option (F1).
  - Before any signal, the guard re-reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` for that one pid.
  - lane-run and lane-kill are box-only tools, so CI doesn't have them, and lane-run's `setsid` detaches the process the same way.
- **F2 design: survivors are found without a /proc scan.**
  - `groupMembers(rec)` snapshots the recorded leader's descendants with their start times. It reads only that leader's own `/proc/<pid>/task/*/children` files, and its descendants' files. serve-own takes the snapshot once the page is verified, and `stopGroup` takes it again right before the signal.
  - `groupProbe(rec)` sends `process.kill(-pgid, 0)` (signal 0, nothing delivered), and only for our own same-boot record. If the leader's pid has been reused, our group is known to be empty: the kernel never hands out a pid that is still a pgid.
  - `stopGroup` sends one guarded group signal and then waits synchronously for the grace period, so it also works in `exit` handlers. Any member still alive with the same start time is a survivor.
  - Survivors are **reported, never signalled again, never dropped**. serve-own and the browser scripts print one `SURVIVORS … surviving pids: <pids>` line and set exit code 3. d2 halts.
- **F3:** every `vite preview` in `scripts/` now goes through `spawnRecorded`/`stopOrReport`. That covers 9 more scripts that had a raw `process.kill(-srv.pid)` or `srv.kill()`. The only places that signal, detach or read `/proc` are the 6 sites in `recorded-pid.mjs` marked `// rule-21 guarded site`.
- **F5 (HoO ruling):**
  - (a) d2 never triggers Playwright's group kill on purpose.
  - (b) If that kill may have fired, d2 halts with the leftover check and `STOP-LIST-for-HoO.txt`, and marks `playwrightKillPossible` in the evidence.
  - (c) The Playwright version is pinned and checked.

| m7 | `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:18-23`: readdir of `/proc` + ppid walk + SIGKILL. `:26,36-37`: `/proc/*/cmdline` match | `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:31-38`: `launch()` uses an exec wrapper that records the PID, plus `guard.watch`. `:54`: `killRecorded(L.rec,'SIGKILL',{group:true})` |
| F1 | `scripts/recorded-pid.mjs:21,36` (58ad41b): `{parent}` option, and `st.ppid !== rec.parent` | `scripts/recorded-pid.mjs:21-27`: no option, parent = `process.pid`. `:35-47`: `rec.parent === process.pid` **and** live ppid `=== process.pid` |

Source check covered 3 files with 4 regexes | All 9 use `spawnRecorded` + `stopOrReport` (`recorded-pid.mjs:123`). `tests/rule21-rules.ts` (14 rules). `tests/rule21-source.test.ts` |
| F4 | `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:46-50` (58ad41b): no leftover check; a refusal only logged | `scripts/d2-guard.mjs:10-44`: `leftovers`, `halt`, `afterKill`. `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:52-56` |
| F7 | `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:16,67` (58ad41b): no try/finally | `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:22-81`: try / catch (halt) / finally (`s1?.stop(); s2?.stop()`) |
| F5 (a) | — | `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs`: plain `ctx.close()` only, through `guard.closeCtx` |
| F5 (b) | — | `scripts/d2-guard.mjs:45-72`: `watch`, `expectExit`, `checkpoint`, `closeCtx` (90 s watchdog that only observes), `haltFor`. `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:45,53,57,63,73,77` |
| F5 (c) | — | `scripts/d2-guard.mjs:74-93` `playwrightPinProblem`. `scripts/d2-kill-browser.mjs:16` exits 2 when Playwright isn't pinned |

| N2 | `tests/recorded-pid.test.ts:17,68`: raw `process.kill` | The tests use `spawnRecorded` + `killRecorded` for their own children |

| F5 (b) | a32faeb | `tests/d2-guard.test.ts`::`F5 (b): … > close() never finishes -> HALT after the observing watchdog; leader ALIVE on STOP-LIST-for-HoO.txt; evidence halted + playwrightKillPossible`, `> close() rejects -> HALT`, `> unexpected disconnect (close event we did not announce) -> checkpoint HALTs; …`, `> an announced exit (our own SIGKILL / closeCtx) is not a halt` |
| F5 (c) | a32faeb | `tests/d2-guard.test.ts`::`F5 (c): Playwright stays pinned > installed playwright-core == package-lock.json version == the version package.json names …` + 3 fake-tree failure cases + 1 pass case |

Tests spawn only their own children: `sleep`, plus `sh -c` wrappers for the grandchild cases. They clean those up by their recorded PIDs. The TERM-ignoring grandchildren are `sleep 2` processes that are no longer our children; they expire on their own, and each test waits for that by PID and start time without signalling them. Every refusal test replaces `process.kill` with a spy that throws.

## Gates (local, node v20.19.2, head a32faeb, clean tree before and after)
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0
- `sync-economy --check`: 0
- Targeted vitest (`--maxWorkers=1`, eng lock + browser lock): 4 files, **104/104 passed**. That's `recorded-pid`, `rule21-source`, `d2-guard` and `serve-own`; serve-own's rc0 chromium case ran because `dist-qa` exists.
- `npm run build` + `check-release-build dist`: 0 (`m4.1+a32faeb`)
- `npm run check-globals -- chromium`: 0, 3/3 PASS. vite stopped through `stopGroup` with no SURVIVORS line, and the ports were closed afterwards.
- d2 smoke on chromium (`DELAYS=0,1000 REPS=1`, `D2_EVIDENCE_DIR` set): SUMMARY 0ms 1/1, 1000ms 1/1, and D3/D4 PASS. After each kill, `afterKill`'s leftover check came back clean. Evidence: `halted:false`, 2 rows, no stop list written. rc 0.
- Not run here: d2 on firefox or webkit (UI QA's QA-R21-D2 run).
- Intermediate commit 6c5919f does not pass tsc (an implicit `any` in a test); 2a8d90a fixes it. Every later head is green.

Review: Architect self-review + green CI + QA verdict (rule 22: Claude is never a gate)
